name: Job-shop scheduling ta50
description: Schedule 30 jobs on 20 machines (job-shop benchmark instance ta50). Every job is a sequence of 20 operations, one on each machine, that must run in the given order; an operation occupies its machine for its whole duration without interruption, and a machine processes one operation at a time. Minimise the makespan, the time at which the last operation ends.
contract: solve(inst) -> starts, a list of n_jobs lists of non-negative integers: starts[j][k] is the start time of operation k of job j. inst has name, n_jobs, n_machines and jobs[j] = list of (machine, duration) pairs in processing order, machines numbered from 0. Operation k + 1 of a job may not start before operation k has ended, and two operations on one machine may not overlap (one may start at the moment the other ends). Score: the makespan, minimized.
notes: Lower bound 1848, best known makespan 1923 (O. Shylo's bounds pages and the ScheduleOpt benchmark library, 2026-11-11).

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Find machine sequences, as start times, of minimum makespan for the open job-shop benchmark instance ta50.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Job-shop scheduling is the canonical model of machine scheduling in manufacturing and is NP-hard in the strong sense; the instances of this family are still open, meaning the best known makespan is above the best proven lower bound, so a shorter schedule is a new best known upper bound.
